summary: Driver catalog hash mismatch prevents SCCM/Intune policy application during provisioning
description: Issue summary: Following a signed driver deployment (catalog v2026.03.10) a subset of corporate laptops began failing policy application from SCCM/Intune. Impact: ~4.7% of devices in us-west report Windows Update error 0x800b0109 and subsequent SCCM policy timeouts, blocking provisioning and onboarding flows. Environment details: Lenovo and Dell corporate fleet, Windows 11 22H2 with security hotpatch rolled 2026-03-10; WSUS/SCCM hybrid, Intune device config enabled. Symptoms: devices reject driver packages citing catalog/certificate verification errors; provisioning agent enters retry loop and fails to reach compliance.
steps_to_reproduce: Provision a corporate laptop in prod-us-west with driver catalog v2026.03.10 applied
Trigger policy sync via Intune or run 'gpupdate /force' and 'wuauclt /detectnow'
Monitor Event Viewer for WindowsUpdate errors and SCCM client logs for policy timeouts
Inspect provisioning-agent logs for 'verification failed (catalog-hash mismatch)' entries
logs: 2026-03-11T03:14:22Z provisioning-agent[pid=412]: apply_driver_pkg: verification failed (catalog-hash mismatch) package=nv_driver_7523.cab
EventLog System 2026-03-11 03:15:01: WindowsUpdate Client 0x800b0109: The certificate for the signer of the message is not valid or is not trusted.
SCCM ccmexec 2026-03-11 03:16:10: ClientPolicyManager: Timeout waiting for policy sync response (attempt 5)
WSUS dp-wsus-03 2026-03-11 03:17:55: CatalogHash lookup: expected=7f3a2c1b, found=4b1e9a5d
investigation_notes: 03/12 09:10 - Triage: Correlated spike in 0x800b0109 with driver rollout wave id=20260310-driver across us-west (~4.7% of fleet)
03/12 10:40 - Hypothesis: CDN/WSUS distribution corrupted catalog during upload causing hash mismatches on clients
03/12 11:22 - Alternate hypothesis: Signing certificate chain rotated but not propagated to all distribution points leading to validation failures
03/12 14:50 - Affected device sample (n=412) shows no strong model-specific pattern; most on firmware 1.06 and corporate docking station but not causative
03/13 08:30 - Reproduced locally by replacing lab WSUS catalog with a corrupted copy; client returned 0x800b0109 and aborted driver install
03/13 12:00 - Replacement of corrupted catalog on DP with golden copy allowed clients to validate and install drivers successfully
comments: 2026-03-12 09:25 Aisha Patel (Reporter): Created ticket after SOC alert and support queue uptick. Attached sample logs and device list.
2026-03-12 10:55 Marcus Green (Assignee): Acknowledged. Pulling distribution point checksums and pausing further driver rollouts.
2026-03-12 14:05 Sofia Chen (SRE): CDN edge reported partial upload for catalog v2026.03.10. Fetching origin copies and revalidating. Recommended marking impacted DPs out-of-service for remediation.

2026-03-13 09:40 Marcus Green: Replaced corrupted catalog on dp-wsus-03 and dp-wsus-07. Test devices validated successfully. About ~60 devices still failing due to cached corrupt entries; preparing client cache purge policy.
2026-03-14 07:18 Aisha Patel: Scheduling cross-team call 08:00 PST to approve SCCM fast-track purge. Noted need for runbook updates and postmortem.
2026-03-14 12:30 Sofia Chen: Drafted infra PR to add checksum preflight for catalog uploads and monitoring alert for catalog validation failures (PR#9893).
resolution_notes: Mitigation 2026-03-13: Replaced corrupted catalog files on affected WSUS distribution points and flagged those DPs out-of-service during sync window

Client remediation 2026-03-13->2026-03-14: SCCM fast-track policy pushed to purge cached catalog entries and force re-download of verified catalog; majority of devices reported compliance within two policy cycles
Full fix 2026-03-14: Added checksum verification to driver release pipeline and deployed monitoring alert to trigger when >0.5% of clients return 0x800b0109 within 24 hours

Follow-ups: Runbook for catalog rollback and client cache purge (owner: Marcus Green, due 2026-03-21); Infra PR to harden CDN upload validation (PR#9893, owner: Sofia Chen); QA to include randomized DP validation before wave start
Impact summary: Internal provisioning delays reduced; ~12 devices required manual re-image due to persistent local corruption. No external customers affected.
